golden-tec.title: Golden Tec
golden-tec.subtitle: Audiovisual installation
golden-tec.short: An interactive installation combining short film, audiovisual elements, and digital technologies to critically explore the effects of hyperconnectivity on the identity and emotions of children and young people. Through Alejandro’s experience, the work invites reflection on the paradox of being constantly connected while experiencing isolation and emotional disconnection.
golden-tec.coverAlt: Provisional still from the animation: a soft 3D scene seen through blue water, with a large cartoon boy's face behind green seaweed and a small fuzzy pink fish in the foreground.

concept.heading: Conceptual description
body: Golden Tec: Interactive Camera is an interactive installation that critically and sensorially explores the impact of hyperconnectivity on the lives of children and young people. Through visual and narrative elements, the work recreates the digital environment surrounding Alejandro, revealing the emotional disconnection that can emerge from constant virtual interaction. With a fragmented and chaotic aesthetic, the installation reflects the anxiety, confusion, and loneliness associated with the illusion of digital connection. The work invites viewers to question how technology influences identity and human relationships, creating a space for critical reflection on the paradox of being more connected than ever while feeling increasingly alone.

statement.title: Artist statement
statement.short: My artistic practice explores the relationships between the body, identity, perception, and the environment through visual, digital, and interactive media. By experimenting with images, narratives, and spaces, I seek to raise questions about sensitivity, vulnerability, and the ways we experience and relate to the world.
long: My practice starts from a simple and difficult question: how the body, identity, perception and the environment intersect. I do not treat them as separate subjects but as parts of a single experience that changes depending on where it is seen from.

I work with visual, digital and interactive media because each allows a different way of approaching that question. I experiment with images, narratives and spaces, and let the process open questions rather than close them.
What I look for is to raise questions about sensitivity, vulnerability and the ways in which we live in the world and relate to it.
